evidence.quote: Tommy was holding the paper thoughtfully.
“Shall we really try it?” he said at last.

adjudications.reason: In the revision, Tuppence's speech (p70) leads straight into 'he said at last' (p71). The source's pause, where Tommy holds the paper thoughtfully, is gone, so 'at last' has no interval to close. The beat also marks slow Tommy deciding to take the scheme seriously, which sets up the uncertain toast. It sits in the required ad-and-toast section and was never listed as optional.

evidence.quote: “Funny scraps one does overhear,” murmured Tommy. “I passed two Johnnies in the street to-day talking about some one called Jane Finn.
Tuppence deftly ensconced herself in one of the vacant seats.
I happened to overhear part of your conversation with the young gentleman in Lyons'.

adjudications.reason: The plan explicitly authorizes cutting p23 and states that p24 can follow without it. Tommy's line works as a self-contained aside, and the name is still planted and then passed over by the seat-grab, so the dependency for Ch. III is met. Whittington's 'overhear' in Ch. III refers to their own conversation, not the café scraps, so this clause plants nothing for it. The omission is a legitimate tradeoff within the budget.

evidence.quote: Remember, I haven’t seen you since that time in hospital in 1916.
Promoted to sweeping out wards, where I found a friend of my childhood in Lieutenant Thomas Beresford (bow, Tommy!).
Good old hospital--demobbed like everything else, I suppose?

adjudications.reason: The hospital frame survives in the lines immediately before the biography. Tommy asks to catch up because he hasn't seen her 'since that time in hospital in 1916', and earlier he says 'Good old hospital'. The biography itself keeps 'sweeping out wards' and finding Lieutenant Beresford there, so the required reunion is recoverable. Restoring the full sentence would cost 26 words that net-zero cannot absorb without cutting other required material, so this is a tolerable tradeoff.

remaining_concerns: Net change is about +1 word against the 1400 target.
The biography still lacks an explicit hospital setting at its opening. The setting is inferable from the adjacent context but slightly abrupt after the parentage line.
